correspondence.component_scope: chosen_eastern_opening_and_southwestward_approach
correspondence.finding: The opening lies in small-lake and narrow-stream terrain south of the main long-lake valley. The detailed image distinguishes partly ice-covered ponds, small connecting reaches and a southwestward valley channel. Several local watercourses are visible, but the complete chosen initial sequence is not independently established and no source-lake or tributary name is assigned.

correspondence.component_scope: westward_upper_transfer_and_northward_turn
correspondence.finding: The selected route turns west and then north across pond-studded, ridge-and-depression terrain. The two images show the nearby westward channel and multiple small northern waterbodies, but do not demonstrate the selected through-connection between them. This is a material corridor-connection gap, not a demand to match exact banks or every model vertex; no alternative route or flow direction is asserted.

correspondence.component_scope: northward_valley_and_southern_lake_approach
correspondence.finding: Farther north, the image depicts a continuous incised valley with tributary junctions leading into the southern end of the first long lake. This supports the downstream valley and lake-entry correspondence at ordinary corridor scale, while leaving the earlier westward-to-northward transfer unresolved. No unsupported name is assigned to this feeder.

correspondence.component_scope: lac_watts_passage
correspondence.finding: The selection follows the elongated southern lake in the Watts–Françoys-Malherbe valley. The original drainage figure labels Lac Watts and the author describes the two lakes in the same glacial valley. Imagery shows the long waterbody, southern entry, side tributary mouths and northern narrowing. Its partly ice-covered appearance does not establish the scene date or present lake conditions.

correspondence.component_scope: inter_lake_channel_and_francoys_malherbe
correspondence.finding: The image visibly connects the northern end of the southern long lake through a broad channel with bars and side joins to the second long lake, then along that lake to its northern outlet. The original authorial valley description identifies the second lake as Françoys-Malherbe. The adjacent western lake and other side waters are not included merely because they are nearby.

correspondence.component_scope: northern_junction_lower_deception_and_actual_terminal
correspondence.finding: The northern lake outlet meets the substantial east-arriving river corridor. The resulting channel runs west through broad alluvial bends to a widening marine inlet. The original Figure3 independently labels the receiving Déception corridor and Baie Déception within Hudson Strait drainage. The image exposes the joined lower channel, coastal mouth and inlet; it does not establish an exact tidal boundary, a surveyed shoreline or present navigation conditions.

correspondence.component_scope: Chosen northwestern opening, eastward dry wash and southwestward bend
correspondence.finding: The detail image shows the chosen opening within a pale, branching dry drainage corridor. That corridor turns east and then southwest through the same widening wash and fan setting represented by the first three selected parts. Its small bends do not require the supplied generalized line to match individual channel edges. No separate name is established for this opening feeder.
correspondence.name_scope: Unnamed selected upper feeder of the representative Sacanana system; no local scalar name assigned.

correspondence.component_scope: Southeastern feeder continuation and join to the broader north–south valley
correspondence.finding: The pale feeder continues southeast through a narrower drainage hollow to the broad east–west alluvial strip, then meets the larger north–south valley. The overview shows its southward continuation through darker vegetated and meandering channel tracts. The joins are visible as connected drainage corridors; a wet surface on the date of inspection is not required or asserted.
correspondence.name_scope: Connected feeder and upper Sacanana-system valley; exact name-start point unassigned.

correspondence.component_scope: Southward valley, intervening wetland-like flats and road crossing
correspondence.finding: The image depicts a sinuous channel within the south-trending valley, widening dark floodplain patches and a continuation toward the major road crossing. The selected sequence stays in this connected valley and reaches its southeastward exit onto the plain. Adjacent small water patches are not substituted for the through-corridor.
correspondence.name_scope: Representative upper Sacanana corridor, without assigning names to individual wetland patches or side channels.

correspondence.component_scope: Southeastward plain entry and eastward alluvial passage
correspondence.finding: The valley opens into a broad, pale alluvial corridor that turns east across the plain. The actual image shows the upstream entry, sinuous middle course and widening pale/vegetated low ground at the next junction. This is correspondence to the drainage landform, not an inference from a basin outline.

correspondence.component_scope: Short middle joins through the widened alluvial and wetland-like tract
correspondence.finding: All four short selected parts occupy the same continuous eastward alluvial strip. Side drainage joins and broad pale low-lying patches are visible; no independently named intervening lake or managed connector is established. The selected short joins do not jump to a separate basin.
correspondence.name_scope: Arroyo Sacanana middle alluvial corridor; wetland and branch names unassigned.

correspondence.component_scope: Meandering lower plain south of Gan Gan and eastern narrowing
correspondence.finding: The lower detail resolves a pale, meandering channel crossing the plain south of the compact settlement and its northern shallow-lake complex. The selected generalized arc follows that same eastward alluvial corridor, then the low passage near the eastern edge of the settlement setting. Its locally displaced bends are ordinary corridor-scale generalization, not evidence for a separate river. EDiPA independently describes Sacanana passing near Gan Gan on its way to Laguna Verde.
correspondence.name_scope: Arroyo Sacanana lower corridor; the nearby Gan Gan lake complex is not assigned as a selected river passage.

correspondence.component_scope: Southeastern terminal approach and entry into the enclosed lake basin
correspondence.finding: The overview shows the lower drainage continuing southeast through pale alluvial ground to the northwestern side of a broad enclosed lake/playa basin. The final river approach and basin entry correspond to the selected route. EDiPA identifies the terminal of Sacanana as Laguna Verde near Chacay Oeste, supporting the name of this receiving basin in the full regional sequence.
correspondence.name_scope: Arroyo Sacanana approach to Laguna Verde; no assertion of perennial discharge.

correspondence.component_scope: Actual selected endpoint within the terminal lake/playa basin
correspondence.finding: The final two selected parts extend south within the eastern sector of the same enclosed pale lake/playa basin. The supplied endpoint is inside that basin, rather than on a depicted onward outlet. This terminal is recorded as a lake-floor/terminal-basin passage, not renamed as a river reach and not extended beyond the actual selected endpoint.
correspondence.name_scope: Laguna Verde terminal-basin passage; distinct waterbody role within the representative Sacanana system.

correspondence.component_scope: Chosen eastern headward opening only
correspondence.finding: The short selected opening runs generally north to the start of the westward inland fragment. Neither the opened conservation-site prose nor the university study covers this headward through-link. No name is assigned from nearby labels or search snippets.

correspondence.component_scope: Westward upper course and its later northwestern turn
correspondence.finding: The selected course continues west, bends southwest and then northwest before meeting the lower fragment. Permitted primary evidence does not establish its full valley correspondence or its connection to the receiving Iscuandé river. Potential El Turbio and Bracito identities are discovery leads only and are not adopted as component names.

correspondence.component_scope: Receiving lower-river/delta lead, not a name proven for every part of this fragment
correspondence.finding: WHSRN explicitly identifies the Iscuandé delta at Santa Bárbara de Iscuandé and describes river-sediment islands, tidal mudflats and mangroves. Cuervo Ferrin identifies that delta as a coastal study area distinct from PNN Sanquianga. These facts provide coastal context, but do not independently trace the complete northward selected course or its actual final channel to the sea.

correspondence.component_scope: Chosen Georgia opening and southward approach north of Eason
correspondence.finding: The chosen opening is on a small mapped broken-line tributary east of the upper Aucilla channel. This approach joins the named Aucilla corridor near the Georgia 122 crossing and continues through a widened water body bearing an Aucilla River label. The upper mapped stream network, widening and southward floodplain establish the ordinary through-sequence; the opening tributary is not separately named here.
correspondence.name_scope: Unnamed selected feeder followed by the named Aucilla River corridor. The widened water body is not assigned an invented lake name.

correspondence.component_scope: Eason, Howell Sink and Boston pond/wetland reach
correspondence.finding: The northern source maps Aucilla River approaching Eason, the Howell Sink passage west of Boston, and the eastward continuation to Massey-Ferguson Pond. The river emerges from the pond setting and bends southeast through a repeatedly labeled Aucilla wetland corridor south of Boston. Broken-line reaches and pond passages are read as the mapped river system, without requiring continuous visible surface water at every selected position.
correspondence.name_scope: Aucilla River representative corridor, with Howell Sink and Massey-Ferguson Pond retaining their own feature identities.

correspondence.component_scope: Georgia–Florida border and upper Aucilla Swamp
correspondence.finding: Overlapping northern and middle originals show the selected southeastward river corridor entering Aucilla Swamp across the state boundary. Tributary channels including the Connel Creek approach join the same named wetland drainage. Repeated Aucilla River labels and the mapped longitudinal wetland/watercourse continue toward the lake reach; this is a supported wetland passage at ordinary corridor scale, not a claim of a single presently open navigable channel.
correspondence.name_scope: Aucilla River through Aucilla Swamp; adjacent ponds and tributaries are not scalar-renamed.

correspondence.component_scope: Sneads Smokehouse Lake and downstream wetland passage
correspondence.finding: The middle original depicts the named river entering Sneads Smokehouse Lake, leaving its southern end, and continuing down the elongated floodplain. The selected route follows this lake-through-river corridor. Nearby Razor Lake, Windom Lake and Parker Pond are distinguishable neighboring features and are not substituted for the selected through-passage.
correspondence.name_scope: Aucilla River system through the distinctly named Sneads Smokehouse Lake.

correspondence.component_scope: Little Aucilla junction, US 90 and Interstate 10 corridor
correspondence.finding: The named Aucilla continues south past the Gum Creek entry. Little Aucilla River approaches from the east near US 90 and joins the main river; the selected mainstem proceeds through the Aucilla settlement and Interstate 10 crossing. Wolf Creek and other side drainage remain lateral tributaries. The visible river links the upper wetland/lake section to the lower channel.
correspondence.name_scope: Aucilla River mainstem with distinct Little Aucilla River tributary.

correspondence.component_scope: Lower channel bends and approach to the sinks
correspondence.finding: The lower original follows the southwestward Aucilla bends through the Alligator Creek and Rocky Creek junction setting, highway crossing, Walker Spring vicinity and lower forested floodplain. Repeated Aucilla labels follow the continuous river into the sink-area approach east of the separate Wacissa River. The selected route does not switch to the parallel Wacissa trunk.
correspondence.name_scope: Aucilla River lower corridor; side creeks and spring features retain separate identities.

correspondence.component_scope: Aucilla sinks, resurgences and Wacissa joining setting
correspondence.finding: The terminal original depicts the named Aucilla corridor as a sequence of broken river reaches and pools continuing toward Nutall Rise. DEP’s independently issued conservation-project description explicitly identifies repeated underground and surface flow in the Aucilla River Sinks. The earlier-read SRWMD program prose identifies Nutall Rise as the final resurgence and Wacissa as a braided tributary. The map shows that tributary/canal network separately to the west and its connection to the lower Aucilla near the resurgence. Together these sources establish the ordinary karst through-passage and receiving-river identity without treating each underground interval as an open channel.
correspondence.name_scope: Aucilla River karst system. Wacissa River and Slave Canal are distinct neighboring/joining features; no present flow allocation or canal-operation claim.

correspondence.component_scope: Nutall Rise to Mandalay and the actual coastal terminal
correspondence.finding: The terminal original shows the resumed Aucilla crossing US 98, passing Ward Island and Mandalay, and continuing through the coastal marsh to its mapped open-water mouth. The selected final part reaches this river outlet; it does not end at a lake, inland swamp or the Wacissa junction. The previously read official program prose identifies the receiving coastal water as the Gulf of Mexico. Neighboring Econfina River and marsh creeks remain separate outlets.
correspondence.name_scope: Lower Aucilla River and its coastal mouth; the Gulf is not assigned a river scalar name.
